chunks: They will say, 'Glory be to You! You are our protector rather than them. In fact, they worshipped the jinn; most of them believed in them.'

key_terms.سُبْحَانَكَ: Glory be to You (an expression of exaltation and acknowledgment of God's superiority)
key_terms.مُؤْمِنُونَ: Believers (in the context of believing in the jinn as deities)

ai.seo_question: Who did the polytheists actually worship according to this verse?
ai.summary: In the Hereafter, polytheists disown their idols, attributing their misguidance to the jinn, whom they followed as intermediaries. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of how human belief in jinnic influence facilitated idolatry, serving as a divine test where jinn acted as guides for those who believed in them. The verse highlights the shift from worshipping physical idols to recognizing the spiritual authority of jinn, who were more 'believable' due to their unseen nature.
